answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, each identity locks its own refundable smart-contract bond, making multiple identities costly. This mechanism requires a slash to occur only when cryptographic proof shows conflicting commitments signed for the same task. Like a cedar tree's unique growth rings, each identity's bond serves as a distinct identifier. In an orchard of competing identities, this mechanism ensures that only one can claim ownership. Meanwhile, a ferrous metal's magnetic properties can be used to detect and prevent conflicting commitments, maintaining the integrity of the system.
